story: As a new user, I want to register with a username, email and password so that I can have my own private workflow space.
acceptance: Registration returns a token; weak passwords and duplicate emails are rejected.

story: As a registered user, I want to log in and log out so that only I can access my workflow items.
acceptance: Login returns a token; logout invalidates it; wrong password is rejected.

story: As a user, I want to create a workflow item with a title and description so that I can record the work I need to do.
acceptance: A blank title is rejected; the new item starts as Pending.

story: As a user, I want to change an item's status (Pending, In Progress, Completed) so that I can track my progress.
acceptance: Only the three valid statuses are accepted; the change is saved.

story: As a user, I want to edit an existing item so that I can correct or improve its title and description.
acceptance: Edited values are saved and shown immediately.

story: As a user, I want to delete completed or outdated items so that my list stays relevant.
acceptance: A confirmation is shown; the item is removed; other users' items cannot be deleted.

story: As a user, I want to filter my items by status so that I can focus on what is still open.
acceptance: Filtering by each status returns only matching items.

story: As a developer, I want a GitHub repository with feature branches, pull requests and a Kanban board so that work is organised and reviewed before merging.
acceptance: main is protected; every change is merged by a reviewed pull request.

story: As a DevOps engineer, I want a Dockerfile for the Django backend so that it builds the same way on every machine.
acceptance: docker build succeeds; the container answers /api/health/.

story: As a DevOps engineer, I want a Dockerfile for the React frontend so that the user interface is packaged and served consistently.
acceptance: docker build succeeds; the image serves the built site.

story: As a developer, I want a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every push and pull request so that broken code is found before it is merged.
acceptance: The workflow runs tests and builds both images; the run is green.

story: As a security-conscious developer, I want configuration and secrets kept in environment variables so that no secret is stored in the repository.
acceptance: No secret key in Git; .env is ignored; CI and Docker read values from variables.

story: As a team lead, I want a CircleCI pipeline for the same repository so that the two CI tools can be compared on real evidence.
acceptance: CircleCI builds and tests the project and builds both Docker images successfully.

story: As a developer, I want Docker Compose to start the whole stack so that I can run the full application locally with one command.
acceptance: docker compose up --build starts frontend and backend.

story: As a developer, I want automated backend and frontend tests in the pipeline so that regressions are caught automatically.
acceptance: The pipeline fails when a test fails.

story: As a developer, I want dependency and Docker layer caching in the pipeline so that builds finish faster and use fewer free minutes.
acceptance: A second run is faster than the first.

story: As a release manager, I want the pipeline to publish tagged images to a container registry so that deployments can pull tested images.
acceptance: Images are pushed only from main with a version tag.

story: As a team member, I want a build-status badge in the README so that everyone can see the health of main at a glance.
acceptance: Badges for both CI tools appear in README.md.
